Someone with a strong aptitude for implicit learning might be better at absorbing the underlying structure of a language just by exposure, even without conscious effort.

Another factor is something called “phonological memory.” This is our ability to store and manipulate speech sounds. People with good phonological memory often find it easier to distinguish between different sounds in a language and to remember new words.

And of course, motivation and learning style play a huge role. Someone who is deeply motivated to learn a language, and who has a learning style that aligns with the way the language is being taught, is likely to progress more quickly.

It's also worth noting that "fast" is relative! Even those who seem to learn quickly are still engaging in a lot of subconscious processing and pattern recognition. It’s just that they might be more efficient at it.
